subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a molecule of BF3?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape with 120° bond angles.

questions.q: Which molecule has a trigonal planar shape?
questions.explain: BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, giving a trigonal planar shape; the others all have a lone pair.

questions.q: Even when a reaction has ΔG < 0, it may not proceed at a measurable rate because:
options: The activation energy is high (kinetic, not thermodynamic, limitation)
questions.explain: Feasibility is thermodynamic; a high activation energy can still make the rate negligibly slow.

questions.q: The ion CO3^2- has which shape?
questions.explain: The carbonate ion has 3 bonding regions around the central carbon and no lone pairs on it, giving a trigonal planar shape (120°).

questions.q: Why does iodine sublime easily at relatively low temperatures?
options: It is a simple molecular solid with weak van der Waals forces
questions.explain: Iodine forms a simple molecular lattice held together only by weak van der Waals forces, which are easily overcome.

questions.q: Why is ice less dense than liquid water?
options: Hydrogen bonds hold molecules in an open lattice
questions.explain: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in a regular open lattice with larger spaces, making it less dense than liquid water.

questions.q: Which molecule is linear?
questions.explain: CO2 has two bonding regions (two double bonds) and no lone pairs on carbon, giving a linear shape with a 180° bond angle.

questions.q: Which species contains a dative (coordinate) covalent bond?
questions.explain: In NH4+ one N–H bond forms because the lone pair on nitrogen is donated to an H+ ion, making it a dative covalent bond.

questions.q: Why is the second electron affinity of oxygen endothermic?
options: Energy is needed to add an electron to an already negative O⁻ ion against repulsion
Oxygen has a full outer shell
The nucleus attracts the electron strongly
questions.explain: Adding an electron to a negative O⁻ requires overcoming repulsion, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: A reaction with ΔH > 0 and ΔS < 0 is:
questions.explain: With ΔH positive and ΔS negative, ΔG is always positive, so it is never feasible.

questions.q: In a calorimetry experiment, 50.0 g of water rises by 8.0 °C (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is q?
A reaction is feasible (spontaneous) when:
questions.explain: A reaction is thermodynamically feasible when ΔG is negative.

questions.q: What does 'mean bond enthalpy' refer to?
options: The enthalpy of a bond at absolute zero
The average energy to break a particular bond type, averaged over many compounds
The enthalpy to break one specific bond in one molecule
The energy released when a bond forms in the gas phase
questions.explain: Mean bond enthalpy is averaged across a range of molecules containing that bond.

questions.q: What is the predicted bond angle in a molecule of H2O?
questions.explain: Water has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs; lone-pair repulsion reduces the bond angle to about 104.5°.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in a methane (CH4) molecule?
questions.explain: CH4 has 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around carbon, giving a tetrahedral shape with bond angles of 109.5°.

questions.q: Which of the following has the strongest intermolecular forces?
questions.explain: Butane (C4H10) has the most electrons and the largest surface area, so it has the strongest van der Waals forces of the four alkanes.

questions.q: Permanent dipole-dipole forces arise between molecules that:
questions.explain: Permanent dipole-dipole forces occur between molecules with a permanent net dipole, i.e. polar molecules.

questions.q: Using bond enthalpies, ΔH of reaction equals:
questions.explain: ΔH = energy to break bonds (in) − energy released making bonds (out).

questions.q: Why can graphite conduct electricity?
options: Each carbon has a delocalised electron
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon forms three covalent bonds, leaving one delocalised electron per atom that is free to move and carry charge.

questions.q: Burning 0.0050 mol of a fuel raises 100 g of water by 20.0 °C (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the enthalpy of combustion?
Which substance does NOT conduct electricity in any state because it has no charged particles free to move?
questions.explain: Diamond is a giant covalent structure with all four outer electrons of each carbon used in bonding, so there are no free charge carriers.

questions.q: Which has a higher boiling point and why: butan-1-ol or pentane (similar Mr)?
questions.explain: Butan-1-ol has an O–H group allowing hydrogen bonding, which is stronger than the van der Waals forces in pentane, so it boils higher.

questions.q: What shape does the molecule SF4 adopt?
questions.explain: SF4 has 4 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair based on a trigonal bipyramid, giving a see-saw shape.

questions.q: Why is the first ionisation energy always endothermic?
options: Energy is released removing an electron
Energy must be supplied to overcome attraction between the nucleus and the electron removed
questions.explain: Removing an electron from a gaseous atom requires energy to overcome nuclear attraction.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = +50 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. The temperature at which it becomes feasible is:
questions.explain: At ΔG=0, T = ΔH/ΔS = 50000/100 = 500 K (above this it is feasible).

questions.q: Given ΔHf[CO2] = −394 and ΔHf[H2O] = −286 kJ mol⁻¹, and ΔHc[CH4] = −890 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate ΔHf[CH4] (combustion gives CO2 + 2H2O).
Which type of bonding is present in solid magnesium?
questions.explain: Magnesium consists of positive ions in a sea of delocalised electrons, which is metallic bonding.

questions.q: The standard enthalpy of neutralisation is approximately constant for strong acids and strong alkalis at about −57 kJ mol⁻¹. Why?
options: Water has a fixed heat capacity
The reaction is always H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l)
All acids release the same number of protons
questions.explain: For strong acid/strong base, the underlying reaction is always H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.

questions.q: Entropy is best described as a measure of:
options: The disorder or number of ways energy and particles can be arranged
The energy content of a system
questions.explain: Entropy measures dispersal of energy/matter, i.e. the number of accessible arrangements.

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state, such as O2(g)?
options: Equal to its enthalpy of atomisation
questions.explain: By definition an element in its standard state has ΔHf = 0.
